title: cli/service-settings: judge the whole fetched page when two data-key files differ, and fix the trial notice wording
body:
domain:server#6 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5

Filed from PR #30087 (card #30042, the boot-time data-key trial-open), contract review PASS at `ec16e14d`, 2026-11-04. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade.

Business reason: the boot trial judges only the newest known-marker `sys_secret` row. So:
- In a database holding rows under both keys, the rows under the key that was not chosen still read as unset, with no notice.
- A corrupt newest row fails under both keys, and in production the boot refuses with a key-problem remedy even when an older row would settle the choice.

Reader who acts: `packages/services/service-settings` owner (`chooseKeyFileByTrialOpen`), with `packages/cli` (`serve.ts`, `resolveExistingDataKey`).

## What to do
- Judge the fetched page (up to 10 rows) instead of one row. Pick the key that opens the most rows, and report a database whose rows split between the two keys as a mixed-key boot error that names both paths.
- Notice wording: the two `opens` notices say the chosen file "opens this database's stored secrets". Say what was measured, for example "opens the newest stored secrets".
- Nits from the review: the stale catch comment in `serve.ts` (around lines 5344–5355), the service-settings README line on the file tier, and a JSDoc sentence noting that `resolveExistingDataKey` sets both channels on the real `process.env`.
- Operator docs: one paragraph on the two-file rule (canonical vs. legacy key file, what the boot does when they differ, and the remedy).

Dedupe: `data key trial`, `DataKeyOpensNothingError`, `both-differ`. **New.**
